item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
237
ABPZ20 KNHC 192325
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Oct 19 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Trudy, located a couple of hundred miles west of west-central
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP94):
Showers and thunderstorms are beginning to show signs of
organization in association with a trough of low pressure located
several hundred miles south-southwest of the coasts of Guatemala and
El Salvador. Environmental conditions appear conducive for
development, and a tropical depression is expected to form in the
next day or so as the system moves westward to west-northwestward at
around 10 mph, remaining well offshore of Central America and
southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Katz/Papin

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy Public Advisory Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 200233
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy Advisory Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
...TRUDY BECOMES A REMNANT LOW...
...THIS IS THE FINAL NHC ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.5N 108.0W
ABOUT 160 MI...260 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy 
was located near latitude 19.5 North, longitude 108.0 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is drifting northward, but is expected to move 
slowly to the west-northwest over the next day or so until 
dissipation.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 35 mph (55 km/h) with 
higher gusts.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information on the remnant low 
please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and 
on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Papin

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 200234
TCDEP1
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
Trudy's convection has rapidly vanished over the last 6-9 hours. In 
fact, the latest satellite imagery shows that all deep convection 
associated with Trudy has dissipated, leaving only a weak remnant 
low-level circulation that has become less defined. As a result, 
Trudy no longer meets the criteria of a tropical cyclone, and this 
is the last NHC advisory on this system. The initial intensity is 
estimated at 30 kt assuming additional spin down of the circulation 
from earlier today.  
 
The vortex of Trudy is expected to degrade further as it moves 
slowly in an environment defined by dry mid-level air, increasing 
vertical wind shear, and upper-level convergence. It should be noted 
that diurnally-driven convective pulses are possible over the next 
day or so. However, this activity is expected to remain disorganized 
and insufficient for redevelopment. The remnant low is expected to 
move very slowly to the west-northwest before guidance generally 
agrees in the circulation dissipating within the next 48 hours.
 
For additional information on Post-Tropical Cyclone Trudy, please
see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service,
under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web
at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
